media.alt: No new cases of Congo virus

content.text: "There have been no new cases of the Congo Crimean Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) at the Aga Khan University Hospital (AKUH)," said Dr Arif Rashid Sarwari, Assistant Professor, Department of Medicine, and AKUH. The Hospital has been treating patients with Viral Hemorrhagic Fevers (VHF) for over five years. The Congo virus, a variety of VHF, is a seasonal illness, with cases most often reported from September to December Dr Sarwari also stressed that "the Congo virus is not an airborne disease, and is contracted through tick bite and exposure to an infected animal or infected patient's blood or body fluid secretions."

The Hospital has had two confirmed deaths over the past three weeks due to the Congo virus. One of these, an AKUH nursing assistant, was corroborated by the Center for Disease Control and Prevention in Atlanta, USA. This nursing aide had been caring for a patient who was later clinically confirmed to have also died from the Congo virus.

Four patients currently admitted to AKUH are under evaluation and are being closely monitored. None of the patients are in a critical condition, including a heath care worker from AKUH, who is making a satisfactory recovery. AKUH has arranged the testing of blood samples of all these four patients by the Center for Disease Control and Prevention in Atlanta to rule out the possibility of CCHF.
